findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify Arm B's fallback for an AC not resolvable from repository evidence — either add an explicit third emit state (e.g. ABSTAIN / INSUFFICIENT) with a rule for how it is scored against ground truth, or state verbatim in the frozen prompt how the agent must classify such ACs (and how such verdicts are excluded from / counted in the false-PASS/false-FAIL tallies the GO rule uses).
evidence: Arm B instruction: 'verify each AC and emit JSON {ac, verdict: PASS|FAIL, citations[]} with file:line evidence' — a strict binary with no insufficient/abstain state.

The guanaco experiment comment on viral-peppy-lowchen (b4be), failure mode #2: 'ACs asserting runtime outcomes ("suites pass green", ... "lint clean") or store-side artifacts (ticket comments) rationally ABSTAIN (45c1, 0e68: 0%)' — the corpus contains ACs Arm B cannot resolve from repo evidence.

The production verifier schema (completion_verdict.schema.json) carries evidence_sufficient/verdict_obtainable markers, and the guanaco filter used a PASS/ABSTAIN-only contract, showing the system deliberately models 'no obtainable verdict' rather than forcing a binary.
The GO rule (i) 'Arm B false-PASS = 0' and (ii) 'Arm B total false-FAILs < Arm A' are directly moved by a fabricated verdict on an unresolvable AC.
findings.finding: Arm B's frozen emit contract ({ac, verdict: PASS|FAIL, citations[]}) defines no fallback/abstain state for an AC whose evidence is not reachable by repository tools, forcing the agent to fabricate PASS or FAIL on exactly the ACs the corpus documents as un-resolvable — contaminating the false-PASS/false-FAIL counts the GO rule depends on.
findings.location: Arm B (treatment) section: 'emit JSON {ac, verdict: PASS|FAIL, citations[]}'; corroborated by Non-goals + the GO rule thresholds
scenarios: Arm B runs on 45c1 or 0e68, hits a runtime-outcome or operator-attested AC with no repo-readable evidence, and — having no abstain option — emits PASS (a false-PASS that breaks GO rule i) or FAIL (a false-FAIL inflating the count GO rule ii compares).
A reviewer cannot distinguish an Arm B 'FAIL' meaning 'refuted' from 'FAIL' meaning 'could not find evidence', so the per-AC verdict table conflates refutation with insufficiency.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define Arm B output-contract failure handling: how a malformed/missing/timed-out subagent verdict is recorded (e.g. re-dispatch once, then record as 'no-verdict' distinct from PASS/FAIL) and how it counts in the GO/NO-GO arithmetic.
evidence: 'emit JSON {ac, verdict: PASS|FAIL, citations[]} with file:line evidence'
Absence: no rule for malformed/missing output, retry, or how an un-emitted AC verdict is scored (as FAIL? as missing? re-run?)
GO rule (i) 'Arm B false-PASS = 0' and (ii) false-FAIL comparison depend on a complete per-AC verdict set
findings.finding: Arm B has no defined handling for a subagent that fails to emit valid JSON, times out, or returns no verdict for an AC — the plan specifies the emit contract but not what happens when the free local harness violates it, which is a data-collection failure mode affecting the per-AC verdict tables (AC2) and the GO/NO-GO arithmetic.
findings.location: Arm B section / Acceptance criteria ('per-AC verdict tables')
scenarios: Copilot subagent emits prose instead of JSON, or omits an AC — the verdict table has a hole and the false-FAIL/false-PASS counts are ambiguous
A timed-out Arm B run leaves a ticket-variant with no rep, silently degrading coverage

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Acknowledge the model/provider confound (Arm B non-Bedrock vs Arm A Bedrock) in the plan and scope the GO claim accordingly — e.g. state that the GO tests 'external-harness-agent-on-its-own-model' as a bundle, or add a same-model minimal-loop reference so a harness win is separable from a model win.
evidence: Hypothesis: 'the unreliability ... lives in OUR in-process scaffolding ... not in the task'
Arm B: 'Copilot CLI task agent; free, non-Bedrock'; Arm A runs on Bedrock (Arm A Bedrock spend tracked)
GO consequence: 'pursue an external-harness verifier SEAM in production design' — attributes the win to the harness, not the model
Clause (iii) 'Arm B median wall time <= 2x Arm A' compares a free local harness on a different model against Bedrock wall time
findings.finding: The two arms differ in BOTH the scaffolding AND the model/provider (Arm B = Copilot CLI, non-Bedrock; Arm A = Bedrock Sonnet), but the hypothesis and the GO consequence attribute any Arm B advantage to the harness/scaffolding seam ('pursue an external-harness verifier seam in production design'). The predeclared GO rule's false-FAIL delta (ii) and median-wall-time <=2x (iii) therefore conflate a harness effect with a model/provider effect — a GO could be earned by a faster/better model rather than by the scaffolding change the experiment claims to isolate.
findings.location: Arms (Arm B), Predeclared decision rule (clauses ii and iii)
scenarios: Arm B wins (ii)/(iii) chiefly because the Copilot CLI runs a faster or stronger model, and the operator reads it as evidence the harness seam is the fix
A same-model, minimal-scaffold loop on Bedrock might have shown no harness benefit, but that comparison is never made
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence under Arms/decision-rule noting the arms vary model+harness together, and either (a) reframe the GO consequence as evaluating the whole external-harness-agent bundle rather than 'the harness seam' specifically, or (b) add a third reference point: the same minimal free-tool loop pointed at the same Bedrock model Arm A uses, so wall-time and false-FAIL deltas attributable to scaffolding are isolable from model differences.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how Arm A $ spend is computed (e.g. Bedrock token counts × the model's published per-token rate, or the account billing readout) so the $20 stop-rule and AC5 are reproducible.
evidence: 'Arm A Bedrock spend (tokens + $)'
'track cumulative spend per run and STOP dispatching Arm A runs at the cap'
Absence: no mapping from tokens to $ (rate card / pricing source) is stated, yet the STOP decision and AC 5 ('Bedrock spend ≤ $20 documented') depend on it
findings.finding: The $ figure for Arm A Bedrock spend has no stated computation source or protocol — the plan names 'tokens + $' and a $20 cap with 'track cumulative spend per run' but never says how dollars are derived (token counts × which rate card, or a billing readout).
findings.location: Metrics section / Budget & reps ('track cumulative spend per run and STOP ... at the cap')
scenarios: Executor reaches ~$20 but cannot decide whether to stop because the token→$ conversion is undefined
Two runs compute spend differently, making the cap enforcement non-reproducible
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'Arm A $ = input+output token counts per run × the Bedrock per-token price for the model in use; cumulative $ summed across dispatched runs.'

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the exact Copilot CLI subcommand/flags used to dispatch a non-interactive per-ticket task-agent (observed from `--help`, not memory), confirm it can be pinned to the worktree path and coerced to emit parseable JSON, and record the evidence class (MATCH/MISMATCH/UNVERIFIED) before the first Arm B run.
evidence: Plan: 'a FRESH local harness subagent (Copilot CLI task agent; free, non-Bedrock) receives ONLY... the instruction to verify each AC and emit JSON {ac, verdict: PASS|FAIL, citations[]} with file:line evidence'
Repo confirms Copilot CLI exists as a harness surface (.github/copilot-instructions.md; scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py) but NO plan text names the task-agent subcommand/flags
Evidence class: Partially-verified (vendor/CLI exists; the specific task-agent + JSON-emission surface is unconfirmed)
ABSENCE: no --help-grounded subcommand/flag observation; JSON-output capability inferred, not verified
findings.finding: Arm B depends on a 'Copilot CLI task agent' capability that is asserted but never verified against --help/docs: no subcommand or flag is named for dispatching a non-interactive per-ticket subagent, and the plan does not confirm the CLI can accept a frozen prompt + worktree path and emit parseable JSON {ac, verdict, citations[]}. The Copilot CLI surface exists in this repo (copilot-instructions.md; scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py notes its skill-drop behavior), so the integration exists, but the specific invocation surface is UNVERIFIED — and the entire GO/NO-GO rule rides on Arm B behavior.
findings.location: Arms → Arm B (treatment): minimal harness agent
scenarios: Copilot CLI has no scriptable non-interactive task-agent mode, or cannot be pinned to a worktree path, so Arm B cannot be dispatched programmatically per ticket
The CLI cannot be coerced to emit clean parseable JSON, so per-AC verdict tables can't be built and the GO/NO-GO arithmetic is uncomputable
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-command Arm-B probe as a pre-step: run the Copilot CLI task-agent on ONE corpus ticket, capture the exact invocation + raw JSON output, and record it on the ticket; only then freeze the prompt and start reps.
